newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, slight growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, slight growth ahead.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in buoyant trade on Tuesday and market participants forecast a slight upward movement in prices and continued good activity.
"I expect a somewhat livelier trade to continue with the general upward trend in prices," analyst Denis Fuduric of Investment Bank Austria told Reuters.
But another trader foresaw little change in the week ahead.
"We see some more buying now, but I believe most prices will only fluctuate within a five percent range," Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage said.
Seven of 16 active issues rose, five fell and four were flat. Volume rose to 20,299 from 9,249 units and turnover doubled to 7.6 million kuna.
Croatia Banka took the spotlight adding 30 kuna (or 20 percent) to 180 kuna, on volume of 2,770 shares.

"The word is that they will pay handsome dividends which might push the price up some more before the annual meeting, with slight correction later on", Fuduric said. The bank is about to publish its annual results on Friday.

Blue chip Pliva pharmaceutical was the day's most active stock with 4,052 shares sold. It closed 1.6 percent lower at 493 kuna and its Global Depository Receipts in London fell to $16.46 from $16.55 on Monday.
But traders said the company was only stabilising after a guick rise following the news that it was about to take over the Polish drugs frim Polfa.
"Large volumes of trading may indicate a mild rise that could go on until the summer," said Fuduric.
Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka was flat at 2,000 kuna with 488 shares changing hands. Its GDR's traded at $32.87-$33.0 range on London's Seaq International.
Food stock Podravka was flat at 275 kuna with 2,938 units sold, while Karlovacka Pivovara brewerey continued its recent rise adding 20 kuna to 440 selling 967 shares.
The brewerey where Chile's Cervecerias Unidas have a majority stake, posted significant gains in the past weeks, and traders said its growth was likely to continue at a slower pace.
Three of five active hoteliers ended lower, one was flat and one rose with no significant changes foreseen before September.
* Biggest decliner was hotelier Istraturist losing nine kuna (or 4.7 percent) to 181 kuna with 2.682 shares sold.
* Most active issue was fully-listed drugs company Pliva which fell 14 kuna to 493 kuna, selling 4,052 shares. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
